stated: The Conservative Party will improve the experiences of children in social care by creating more places in children’s homes, prioritising kinship care, supporting adoptive families, and assisting care leavers with housing, education, and employment.

source.quote: We will improve the experiences of children in social care, because every child deserves to live in a safe and loving home. We will create more places in children’s homes while prioritising keeping families together where that’s best for the child through our Kinship Care Strategy and helping children grow up in loving adoptive families where that is a better option.

bearing_set.reason: The policy explicitly targets care leavers' education and employment outcomes — a group with severely depressed attainment and skills prospects — earning a real verdict on education and opportunity.
The policy explicitly commits to assisting care leavers with housing, a group at acute risk of homelessness on leaving care, earning a real verdict on affordable/secure housing access.

The policy explicitly assists care leavers with employment; this group faces disproportionately poor employment outcomes, so a targeted intervention directly moves employment-rate and job-quality indicators for this vulnerable cohort.

Care-experienced children are among the most materially disadvantaged cohorts; targeted kinship, adoption, and leaver support narrows intergenerational mobility gaps and the income/opportunity gap between the bottom and the rest — a clear distributional effect on inequality indicators.

membership_note: The policy bears on three fundamentals: educational opportunity and attainment (O7), housing access for care leavers (O1), and inequality/intergenerational mobility (O14). Effects on healthcare (O3) and prosperity (O13) are plausible but too indirect and population-small to clear the non-negligible bar independently.
